title: In-place pharmacological replacement of missing human cell types

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a drug regimen that converts cells already inside a patient into a missing, functional human cell type. It would need to produce enough correctly specified cells to restore a defined physiological function, with control over where conversion occurs and where it stops. The replacement cells would originate within the patient rather than being manufactured outside the body and transplanted.

Conceptual scope: drug exposure must cause the endogenous change of cell identity. Producing stem cells in a dish, transplanting replacement cells, or inducing conversion with genetic reprogramming factors alone would not establish this capability. The proposal does not require conversion to pass through pluripotency; its defining result is a controlled transition to the needed functional identity inside living tissue.

significance.text: Conditional significance: successful endogenous conversion would extend pharmacology from changing the behavior of existing cells to replacing a defined cell population. A suitable local population could become a source of replacement cells, potentially reducing reliance on external cell manufacturing and transplantation. The immediate advance would be restoration of the function supplied by those cells; broader organ recovery would depend on the surrounding tissue remaining capable of supporting them.

The supplied clinical report illustrates why functional cell replacement matters: transplantation of externally produced islets was followed by sustained insulin independence in one person with type 1 diabetes. This provides a clinical foundation for the therapeutic goal, while leaving endogenous drug-induced conversion as a separate proposed achievement.

Conditional limits: avoiding transplanted cells would follow directly from the proposed mechanism, but avoiding surgery would depend on drug delivery. Local administration could still require an invasive procedure. Restoring a cell identity also does not by itself rebuild complex anatomy, establish appropriate innervation, or demonstrate long-term safety. Repeated treatment or use across multiple organs would be downstream possibilities requiring separate evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is controlled conversion of an identified endogenous human cell population into sufficiently numerous, mature and functional replacement cells within living tissue. The clinical source establishes an ex vivo foundation through chemically induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived islets, but its abstract does not describe the chemical induction protocol or show that the same process can operate inside a patient.

Engineering synthesis: a successful regimen would need to reach the intended starting cells, direct them toward the chosen identity, limit conversion of other populations, and stop at an appropriate endpoint. Cell identity would need to include useful physiological behavior, rather than marker expression alone. Conversion would also have to preserve enough of the starting population's original function to avoid exchanging one deficit for another.

Scientific and safety challenges proposed here include establishing endogenous lineage origin, obtaining adequate conversion efficiency, supporting maturation and integration, and maintaining benefit after treatment ends. Inappropriate intermediate states, uncontrolled growth and off-target conversion are concerns that a convincing demonstration would need to assess. The supplied abstract does not establish which of these is the dominant limiting barrier, their frequency, or whether a particular in vivo strategy has overcome them.

current_state.text: Wang and colleagues reported a first-in-human phase I preliminary analysis in Cell, dated October 31, 2024. Autologous chemically induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived islets were transplanted beneath the abdominal anterior rectus sheath in one person with type 1 diabetes. Sustained insulin independence began 75 days after transplantation, and the abstract reports that all study endpoints were met at one year. These are reported clinical outcomes from one patient, rather than projections.

The demonstrated scope is external cell production followed by transplantation and functional benefit. It does not demonstrate drug-induced conversion of endogenous cells inside the patient. The one-patient preliminary analysis provides a reason for further clinical investigation of the transplantation approach, while leaving reproducibility across patients, broader applicability and outcomes beyond the reported follow-up unresolved.

Evidence access is limited to the retained PubMed abstract described in the supplied review. Although the webpage extraction was untruncated and had no recorded extraction issues, it remains partial evidence for the article: the supplied material does not permit independent assessment of the full methods, chemical induction protocol, endpoint definitions or underlying endpoint data. This limits interpretation without negating the abstract's reported results.

Evidence boundary: no human trial of in-place, drug-only cell-fate replacement is documented in the supplied material. The freshness search record is empty, so this packet cannot establish whether the proposed capability remains clinically unachieved as of November 1, 2026, or whether the 2024 transplantation report is the strongest available result. The dated clinical finding remains supported within its stated scope.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: in humans, a drug regimen should convert an identified endogenous cell population into functional cells of a chosen identity, without transplanted cells or an integrating genetic vector. Evidence should attribute the conversion to drug exposure and establish endogenous origin through a credible lineage-attribution strategy. A transplantation result or an animal experiment using genetic reprogramming factors would not satisfy this proposed human pharmacological criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Drugs convert endogenous human cells into functional target cells

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional criterion: the new cells should restore a prespecified physiological deficit, with evidence linking the improvement to their activity. Benefit should persist after drug clearance for an observation period chosen in advance and justified by the tissue and disease. Cell markers alone would be insufficient; the demonstration should assess mature function, sufficient cell numbers and integration appropriate to the target tissue.
completion_criteria.label: Restored physiological function persists after drug clearance

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and safety criteria: independent replication and results across multiple patients should test reliability, while follow-up should assess inappropriate growth, off-target conversion, loss of necessary starting cells and durability. Practical boundaries should specify the eligible starting population, target identity, delivery route, dose range and disease setting. These are proposed criteria, not established standards; finite demonstrations would establish breadth within the tested settings, rather than universal conversion of arbitrary human cell types.
completion_criteria.label: Report independent replication across patients, safety follow-up and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based distinction: PHA-12, “A pharmacological trigger for scarless regrowth of complex adult mammalian structures,” concerns patterned reconstruction of a structure. PHA-06 concerns replacement of a defined cell type. Both could contribute to recovery in one organ, but successful cell replacement would not establish scarless structural regrowth, and structural regrowth alone would not establish the specific endogenous fate-conversion mechanism proposed here. This comparison uses the supplied roster and candidate framing; a detailed PHA-12 research record was not supplied.

Roster-based distinction: PHA-09, “A drug that changes the human aging rate across organ systems,” could overlap with cell replacement if a particular replacement intervention improved age-related dysfunction. Such improvement would not by itself demonstrate a change in aging rate across organs. Conversely, altering aging rate would not necessarily replace a missing cell population.

Roster-based enabling relationships: PHA-05, systemic pharmacological access to brain parenchyma for arbitrary drug classes, could address delivery for some neural replacement strategies. PHA-11, reliable oral systemic exposure for folded peptides and proteins, could matter if a replacement regimen used those agents and required oral delivery. Neither access capability establishes controlled cell-fate conversion, and PHA-06 does not inherently require either delivery route.

Roster-based distinction: PHA-02 concerns predicting human efficacy, dose and major toxicity before first exposure, whereas PHA-06 requires demonstrating a therapeutic conversion in humans. Better prediction could assist development without supplying the conversion mechanism. PHA-13, a medicine that holds its own therapeutic window without an external controller, could overlap with limiting conversion or growth, but that autonomous control is an additional capability rather than a prerequisite built into this concept.

Roster-based distinction: PHA-04 concerns antigen-chosen control of immune memory. Immune context could affect whether replacement cells retain their benefit, but changing immune memory and producing replacement cells are different interventions. Success at one would not establish the other.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish whether human in-place, drug-only cell-fate replacement has been demonstrated or entered clinical testing by November 1, 2026.
Full methods and endpoint data were not available in the supplied review; the chemical induction protocol, detailed safety findings and endpoint definitions remain unassessed here.
The proposed innovation has no specified starting population, replacement identity, drug regimen, delivery route or target disease, so feasibility and dominant barriers remain application-dependent.
A credible human lineage-attribution method, justified post-clearance observation period and adequate replication and safety follow-up would need to be defined for a concrete demonstration.
The detailed PHA-12 record and research records for other roster entries were not supplied; related-concept comparisons therefore remain title-based conceptual mappings.

brief.title: Medicines that replace missing cells inside the body
possible: People who have lost a needed type of cell could regain its function through medicines that turn nearby cells into replacements. The new cells would form inside the body, with treatment controlling where the change happens and when it stops.
why: Medicines could replace missing cells as well as change how existing cells behave. Patients could draw on their own tissue for replacements, reducing reliance on cells grown outside the body and transplanted.

sources.showed: A preliminary human trial reported sustained freedom from insulin treatment after transplantation of laboratory-grown islets, clusters of cells that produce insulin.
sources.quote: The patient achieved sustained insulin independence starting 75 days post-transplantation.
sources.cited_for: Replacing missing cells can restore a useful function in a patient.
sources.not_established: The cells were made outside the body and transplanted; drugs did not convert cells inside the patient.

sources.showed: The team reported that chemicals converted astrocytes, supporting brain cells, into neurons, cells that carry nerve signals, inside adult mouse brains. The new cells had electrical activity and received connections from existing neurons.
sources.cited_for: Chemical treatment can produce a change of cell identity inside living mouse brain tissue.
sources.not_established: This does not establish conversion in humans or restoration of a lost bodily function.

sources.showed: Changing cell metabolism, the chemical processes within cells, gave pancreatic alpha cells features of insulin-producing beta cells. The team reported beta-cell regeneration and improvement in diabetes.
sources.quote: AR inhibition suppresses glycogen synthesis and enhances the pentose phosphate pathway.
sources.cited_for: Changing cell metabolism offers a route toward producing replacement insulin-producing cells.
sources.not_established: The findings do not establish lasting restoration of function through drug-induced conversion inside a human patient.

sources.who: Amanda M Ackermann, Nicholas G Moss and Klaus H Kaestner
sources.showed: Tracking the descendants of pancreatic alpha cells in mice, the researchers found that GABA and artesunate did not stimulate conversion into insulin-producing beta cells or insulin secretion.
sources.quote: neither α-to-β cell trans-differentiation nor insulin secretion were stimulated
sources.cited_for: Some reported drug-induced conversions have failed independent tests that track where the cells came from.
sources.not_established: Failure of these treatments does not establish whether other drug regimens can achieve controlled conversion.

shown: Ma and colleagues reported chemical conversion of supporting brain cells into electrically active nerve cells inside adult mice. Zhang and colleagues reported chemical changes that promoted insulin-producing cell features and improved diabetes.

In humans, Wang and colleagues reported sustained freedom from insulin treatment in one participant after transplanting laboratory-grown cells. This demonstrated functional replacement through transplantation.
missing: A human demonstration must establish that drugs turn cells already in the body into the needed functional cell type.
Enough replacement cells must restore a defined function and sustain it after the drugs leave the body.
Treatment must control where conversion happens and stops, while preserving the necessary functions of the starting cells.
Independent teams must reproduce the benefit across patients and assess unwanted conversion, abnormal growth and lasting safety.

milestones.label: Drugs turn existing human cells into functional replacements
milestones.explanation: A human study would have to trace functional replacement cells to existing cells and establish that drugs caused the change without transplants or inserted genetic instructions. This would establish conversion inside the patient.

milestones.label: Restored function lasts after the drugs leave
milestones.explanation: The new cells would have to restore a defined bodily function for a justified, preset period after the drugs clear. This would demonstrate lasting repair through their activity.

milestones.label: Independent studies establish reliability, safety and practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent studies across patients would have to reproduce benefit, assess lasting safety and define suitable cells, diseases, doses and delivery routes. This would establish where treatment works reliably.

uncertain: Which starting cells, replacement cells and diseases offer a feasible path remains application-dependent.
How best to prove the origin of replacement cells in humans remains an open question.
The appropriate duration of benefit and safety follow-up depends on the tissue and disease.

page.title: In vivo chemical reprogramming for cell replacement
page.definition: A drug given to a patient would convert cells already present in the affected tissue into a different cell type and restore function lost when cells of that type died. In noise-deafened mice, for example, supporting cells in the inner ear gave rise to new sensory hair cells and hearing partly recovered. The drug induces the change inside the body, without a cell transplant or delivery of genetic reprogramming factors.

goal.need: Worldwide, 430 million people need rehabilitation for disabling hearing loss from all causes, including 34 million children. Hearing aids amplify sound for surviving hair cells, yet speech can remain hard to understand in noise. For people whose hearing loss stems from missing hair cells, replacing those cells could restore some ability to detect sound. In type 1 diabetes, enough functioning beta cells could free a person from taking insulin without an islet transplant. Lasting benefit requires the new cells to survive autoimmune attack.

figures.caption: Global need for hearing rehabilitation, reported by WHO on 3 March 2026.
figures.note: Children are included in the total. WHO defines disabling hearing loss as hearing loss greater than 35 dB in the better-hearing ear.

statements.context: The committee lists generating these cells as a future research direction. The goal encompasses genetic and chemical approaches.

completion.title: A confirmatory human trial restores function through drug-induced conversion of resident cells.
completion.criterion: A confirmatory controlled human trial meets its prospectively specified clinical efficacy endpoint for a disease caused by loss of a defined cell type. Evidence establishes that drug exposure converted an identified resident population into functional replacement cells responsible for the benefit, without transplantation or delivered genetic reprogramming factors. Endpoint magnitude, sample size and follow-up are those of the registered disease-specific protocol; no universal conversion percentage or duration is imposed.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; no external completion criterion covering this capability across cell types was located.
completion.basis: Searches of FDA drug-development criteria, the DMICC diabetes strategy, NIDCD plans, the Horizon 2020 REGAIN programme and trial registries found no cross-tissue completion test for drug-induced endogenous cell conversion. The quoted goals concern functional regeneration. This Atlas test therefore combines controlled human benefit with evidence of the defining conversion mechanism, without adding an arbitrary durability period.

milestones.title: Drugs convert lineage-traced resident animal cells into physiologically active target cells.
milestones.criterion: Label the resident source population specifically before drug exposure in a living animal. Identify the label in cells that subsequently express markers of the target type and demonstrate physiological activity characteristic of that type.
milestones.set_by: The lineage-tracing criterion articulated by Leaman, Marichal and Berninger, together with the cell-specific functional comparison used by Ma et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: Endogenous starting cell population should be labelled with high specificity before reprogramming, followed by identification of the label in induced cell types

milestones.title: Drug-induced cell replacement restores a lost physiological function in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: In an animal model with a measured deficit caused by cell loss, show that drug treatment produces replacement cells from an identified resident population and that the corresponding physiological function improves relative to controls. Relate the functional improvement to the replacement cells in the affected tissue.
milestones.set_by: Community convention exemplified by Mizutari et al., who assessed the origin of new cochlear hair cells and measured auditory responses in treated and control ears.
milestones.threshold_quote: new hair cells can be induced and can cause partial recovery of hearing

milestones.title: A first human study of a candidate cell-conversion drug has regulatory and ethics clearance.
milestones.criterion: The proposed study may begin under the applicable regulatory and ethics requirements. In the United States, the investigational new drug application must be in effect and the institutional review board must approve the study. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the study on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the study may begin.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions, for the US requirements. Other jurisdictions apply their own clinical trial authorization and ethics procedures.
milestones.threshold_quote: FDA may also notify the sponsor earlier that clinical investigations may begin, in which case the IND takes effect upon that notification

milestones.title: Participants receive a candidate cell-conversion drug in a Phase I safety study.
milestones.criterion: Administer the candidate drug to participants in an authorized Phase I study for the intended cell-replacement use. The study assesses safety and the drug’s pharmacological effects in humans.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase I Clinical Studies. This is the published clinical-stage definition, not a finding that conversion has occurred.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans

milestones.title: A controlled Phase II study shows preliminary efficacy for a cell-replacement indication.
milestones.criterion: A controlled Phase II study in patients with the target condition shows preliminary evidence of effectiveness for the intended cell-replacement indication on its prespecified efficacy endpoint, using the comparator and assessment time defined in the protocol.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase 2 and Phase 3 Clinical Studies. FDA identifies preliminary evidence of effectiveness in Phase II as preceding Phase III; it supplies no universal numerical efficacy cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: after preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained in Phase 2

milestones.title: Drug-treated cells in culture acquire the identity and a characteristic function of the target cell.
milestones.criterion: Starting with an identified source population in culture, show that drug exposure generates cells with molecular features of the target type and measure a function characteristic of that type. For cardiomyocytes, contraction and electrical activity can be compared with those of native heart muscle cells.
milestones.set_by: Community convention applied by Cao et al. to human fibroblasts and by Ma et al. to mouse astrocytes.
milestones.threshold_quote: uniformly contracted and resembled human cardiomyocytes in their transcriptome, epigenetic, and electrophysiological properties

milestones.title: Nonclinical safety data support the proposed starting dose and design of the first human study.
milestones.criterion: Characterize the candidate drug’s safety profile sufficiently to justify the starting dose and design of the proposed first human study, taking account of the intended population, drug and mechanism of action. For a locally administered candidate, address safety at the site of administration.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions, section 2. The REGAIN programme specified local safety and dosing for its inner-ear candidate.
milestones.threshold_quote: provide a sound basis for the proposed starting dose and study design

not_found: No controlled human study was found that established both drug-induced conversion of resident cells and restoration of their missing physiological function.
The full methods of Zhang et al.'s 7 August 2026 paper were behind subscription access; its abstract and Figure 6 were accessible.

results.detail: The reported results cover selected local histological measures after infusion.

results.finding: In cultured αTC1 cells, 7 days of EPZ011989 induced β-cell gene expression and the study measured glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (n = 3 for secretion).

results.finding: In ME-6-PG-treated mice, the study quantified insulin-positive cells within the traced pancreatic α-cell lineage (4 mice per group).
results.detail: Insulin staining establishes a molecular feature. Glucose-responsive insulin secretion by the traced cells in vivo remains unshown in the excerpt.

results.finding: ME-6-PG promoted β-cell regeneration and alleviated diabetes in mice (10 per group for random blood glucose). The excerpt gives no glucose effect size.
results.detail: The excerpt reports pancreatic regeneration and glycemic improvement alongside one another. It does not establish how much of the improvement came from α-derived replacement cells.
results.quote: Methylated 6-PG treatment induced islet regeneration and alleviated metabolic disorder in diabetic mice.

results.finding: Mouse ME-6-PG studies included organ histology and body-weight monitoring (10 diabetic mice per group for weight). The excerpt gives no toxicity magnitude.
results.detail: The histology caption gives no group size or lesion assessment. The reported serum measurements cover oral, intraperitoneal and intravenous administration.

results.finding: In 19 lineage-traced male mice, 3 months of GABA or artesunate produced no significant increase in insulin-positive α-cell descendants.
results.detail: The study measured plasma insulin at the whole-animal level. Insulin staining identified a molecular marker but did not establish secretion by individual lineage-labeled cells.
results.quote: Our study shows no evidence that artesunate or GABA treatment stimulates α-to-β cell trans-differentiation.

results.finding: In nondiabetic male mice (4 per arm), artesunate lowered plasma glucose versus vehicle at 60 minutes during glucose tolerance testing.
results.detail: Artesunate-treated mice also gained less weight, which the authors identified as a likely explanation for the glucose tolerance result.
results.quote: Mice treated with artesunate for three months demonstrated faster glucose clearance than control mice treated with DMSO, with significantly lower plasma glucose levels at 60 and 90 minutes during intraperitoneal glucose tolerance tests

results.finding: In five PF-562271-treated mice, lineage-traced acinar-derived insulin-positive cells accounted for 1.85% of all β cells.

results.finding: After partial β-cell ablation, 9 of 10 PF-562271-treated mice maintained improved blood glucose through follow-up.
results.detail: The other lineage-traced treated mouse was examined early and had labeled islet cells that had yet to express insulin. The single treated macaque also required less exogenous insulin, but the origin of its insulin-positive cells was undetermined.
results.quote: Importantly, mice that recovered (9/10) showed BG values below 300 mg/dl for the remainder of the study (1 month after FAKi-treatment cessation), at which time the mice were sacrificed.

Threshold recoveries after
LY411575
treatment were significantly greater than control at 8, 11.33 and 16 kHz

results.finding: Noise-deafened mice given oral LY411575 at 50 mg/kg had significant adverse effects (n unreported).
results.detail: The local study used a single drug concentration. The carrier-only hearing readout and treated-ear cell counts provide limited information about local safety.
results.quote: The treated mice suffered significant side-effects

results.finding: In THR-123-treated mouse pancreatic slice culture, five of seven tracked duct-associated cells showed a calcium response to high glucose.
results.detail: The calcium imaging result is from seven selected cells in one imaged field. It establishes glucose responsiveness at the cell level, with incomplete functional maturation.
results.quote: However, several exhibited a clear reaction to high glucose (1-3, 5-6) or KCl-induced depolarization (1, 4).

results.finding: In alloxan-diabetic mice given THR-123 or saline (n=4 per group), 67.56% of insulin-positive pancreatic cells in treated mice incorporated BrdU.
results.detail: Ductal colocalization supports a possible ductal origin. The experiment does not resolve whether pre-existing beta cells contributed through proliferation.
results.quote:
The percentage of insulin
+
cells that were also BrdU
+
in alloxan/THR-123 mice (67.56 ± 12.2%) was significantly higher than that of alloxan/saline animals (15.13 ± 5.44%; p = 0.012) (Fig.
2b
, middle).

results.finding: In mice with established toxin-induced diabetes (n=20 per arm at treatment start), THR-123 lowered blood glucose by up to about 200 mg/dL relative to saline.
results.detail: Treated mice cleared glucose more efficiently and had higher fasting insulin and C-peptide. The Matsuda index showed no significant group difference. The duct-to-beta-cell transition was tracked separately in cultured slices.
results.quote:
As shown in Supplementary Fig.
2c
, THR-123 decreased hyperglycemia vs. controls (maximum glycemic separation of ~200 mg/dL at 16 weeks) and led to normoglycemia by week 20.

results.finding: THR-123-treated diabetic mice showed no detected increase in proliferation across three sampled extrapancreatic organs (sample size unstated).
results.detail: BrdU labeling measures proliferation. The paper gives no proposed human starting dose or study design for THR-123.
results.quote: At any rate, off-target increases of basal proliferation rates could not be detected either in non-diabetic mice or in the extrapancreatic tissues of diabetic mice exposed to THR-123 (see “Results”).

results.finding: LY3056480’s preclinical no-observed-adverse-effect level informed the 25 µg starting dose. The nonclinical sample size was unreported.
results.detail: Formulation solubility and middle-ear volume determined the maximum dose.
results.quote:
We chose a traditional 3 + 3 dose escalation study design, starting
with the ‘no observed adverse effect level’ dose from our pre-clinical
studies and ending with the maximum dose based upon solubility of the
formulation and middle ear volume, over an innovative Phase I design24.

results.finding: REGAIN (59 participants across both phases) received regulatory and ethics clearance covering 3 sites.
results.detail: The first-in-human Phase I cohort enrolled at the UK site. The Athens and Tübingen sites joined for Phase IIa.
results.quote:
The trial protocol was approved by national reg-
ulatory authorities, medical ethical committees and local R&D autho-
rities in London (London, Central REC Committee, REC Number: 17/
LO/0632), Athens (Hellenic Republic Ministry of Heath National Ethics
Committee - Reg. No.: 83052/2018) and Tübingen

results.finding: Among 15 Phase I participants given intratympanic LY3056480, 0 experienced severe or serious adverse events.
results.quote:
In Phase I
(N = 15, 1 site) there were no severe nor serious adverse events.

results.finding: In 44 Phase IIa patients receiving LY3056480, the treated-ear pure-tone threshold changed by −0.46 dB at 12 weeks.
results.detail: The untreated ear was analyzed separately. Individual improvements on secondary measures did not establish efficacy on the prespecified primary endpoint.
results.quote:
For the total population of 44 patients with mild to moderate SNHL,
the primary endpoint was not met, i.e., the mean pure-tone air-con-
duction threshold across 2, 4, and 8 kHz did not change from baseline
to 12 weeks in the treated ear (Fig.2) (estimated change−0.46 dB; 95%
conﬁdence interval [CI] −1.94 to 1.03

results.finding: Swedish ethics and medicines authorities cleared the GABA beta-cell regeneration study, which randomized 35 men.
results.detail: The earlier Phase I study assessed short-term tolerability and hormonal counter-regulation. The article leaves the first-study status for beta-cell replacement unclear.
results.quote: The study was conducted in accordance with the declaration of Helsinki and approved by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (Dnr 2018/200) and the Swedish Medical Products Agency (EudraCT No 2018-001115-73).

results.finding: Among 33 men with longstanding type 1 diabetes who received oral GABA, 9 had elevated AST.
results.detail: Two participants stopped treatment because of transaminase elevations. Trough GABA levels and hormonal responses to induced hypoglycemia were unchanged.
results.quote: Safety concerns included elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in nine subjects, leading to the withdrawal of two subjects.

results.finding: In 33 men with longstanding type 1 diabetes in the efficacy analysis, C-peptide did not improve after 6 months of oral GABA.
results.detail: All three arms received GABA. The study compared active regimens and used each participant’s baseline as a control for C-peptide.
results.quote: However, we observed no increase in either fasting- or stimulated C-peptide levels during the 6 months of GABA therapy.

results.finding: Institutional review boards approved the FX-322 Phase 1b protocol for the study that randomized 23 adults with stable sensorineural hearing loss.
results.detail: The sample size is the Phase 1b enrollment. The approval statement covers both clinical studies.
results.quote: The protocols and amendments were approved by Institutional Review Boards for participating investigators and each patient provided written informed consent.

results.finding: In a 23-participant Phase 1b safety study for stable sensorineural hearing loss, 15 adults received intratympanic FX-322.
results.detail: The primary safety endpoint was assessed at Day 15. Most adverse events were mild and transient. One tympanic membrane perforation resolved spontaneously within 30 days.
results.quote: A single dose of FX-322 in SNHL subjects was well tolerated with mild, transient treatment-related adverse events (n = 15 FX-322 vs 8 placebo).

results.finding: At Day 90, four of six FX-322-treated ears with a baseline word-recognition deficit showed clinically meaningful improvement.
results.detail: The subgroup included four placebo-treated ears. Baseline speech perception was imbalanced between arms, and exploratory audiometric analyses had no multiplicity adjustment.
results.quote: Four of the six FX-322-treated ears showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements from baseline to 90 days in the prespecified WR test, exceeding expected levels of test–retest variability for this measure

results.finding: FDA and UAB IRB clearance preceded the pediatric GABA trial (n=97), which began enrollment in 2015.
results.quote: We had a protracted period (2 years) prior to study launch in order to obtain FDA approval to administer GABA in children (first human trial). The formal study protocol approvals and funding were in place by 2015 and the first patient enrolled 3/2/2015.

results.finding: In the pediatric GABA trial (n=97), investigators recorded six serious adverse events judged unrelated to treatment.
results.quote: There were six unrelated serious adverse events recorded that required uneventful 1–2 day hospitalizations

results.finding: In children with new-onset type 1 diabetes (n=97), neither GABA regimen significantly preserved C-peptide versus placebo over 12 months.
results.detail: The combination reduced glucagon on a secondary endpoint. The trial registry outcomes were updated after study completion to align with the 2015 protocol.
results.quote: The primary outcome, preservation of fasting/meal-stimulated c-peptide, was not attained.

results.finding: In DFGKLRV-treated mouse astrocyte cultures (n = 5 for marker counts), 24.48% of cells were NeuN-positive. Induced neurons fired action potentials.
results.detail: The sample size of five applies to marker quantification. Resting membrane potentials and firing thresholds remained more depolarized than published primary-neuron values, indicating incomplete electrophysiological maturation.

results.finding: In DFGKLRV-treated hemorrhagic mice (n = 5 for histology), 15.7% of lineage-labeled cells were NeuN-positive. Traced induced neurons fired action potentials.
results.detail: Patch-clamp recordings were made in acute brain slices. Mature induced neurons fired repetitively, while immature induced neurons typically fired a single action potential under the same stimulation.

results.finding: In hemorrhagic mice (n = 8 per group), DFGKLRV improved some sensorimotor outcomes versus vehicle by 12 weeks.
results.detail: Circuit tracing supported local integration of induced neurons. Histology and behavior were assessed in different mice, so the study could not link the extent of neuronal replacement to recovery within individual animals.

results.finding: Sweden authorised the oral GABA beta-cell regeneration study on 2018-06-05, with 36 adults planned and a favourable ethics opinion.
results.detail: The registry marks the study as involving prior human use of the drug. The verdict treats the Phase I component for the intended cell-replacement use as the relevant first human study.

results.finding: DFGKLRV-treated mouse astrocyte cultures (n=5 for staining) yielded 24.48% NeuN-positive cells by day 10. Induced neurons fired action potentials.
results.detail: Resting membrane potentials and firing thresholds remained relatively depolarized compared with published primary-neuron data. The text gives no sample size for the culture patch-clamp recordings.
results.quote: In short, our findings show that DFGKLRV rapidly (within 10 days) converts cultured astrocytes into functional neurons.

results.finding: In hemorrhagic mice treated with DFGKLRV (n=5 for histology), 15.7% of lineage-labeled cells expressed NeuN in a single section. Induced neurons fired action potentials.
results.detail: The authors validated minimal labeling of pre-existing neurons. Vehicle-treated mice had almost no cells positive for both NeuN and the lineage label.
results.quote: The conversion efficiency in a single section reached 15.7% ± 1.8% of all the tdTomato-labeled cells (Fig.  4f ).

results.finding: DFGKLRV-treated hemorrhagic mice (n=8 for behavior) improved versus vehicle on 3 sensorimotor tests.
results.detail: Histology and behavior were assessed in different mice, so the study could not relate the number of induced neurons to recovery in individual animals. Other treatment effects could have contributed.
results.quote: Behavioral assessment indicated a partial improvement in sensorimotor performance in ICH mice at 8–12 weeks after reprogramming (Fig.  5f–h ).

results.finding: The Phase I Remygen study in six men with type 1 diabetes received both required Swedish approvals.
results.detail: The ethics approval reference was Dnr 2018/200/1.
results.quote: The study was approved by both the Uppsala County Ethics Board (Dnr 2018/200/1) and the Swedish Medical Products Agency.

results.finding: Six men with long-standing type 1 diabetes received Remygen in Phase I, with zero serious adverse events.
results.detail: Fasting and stimulated C peptide were unchanged during short-term treatment.
results.quote: During the trial there were no serious and only a few, transient, adverse events reported.

results.finding: LY3056480 started at 25 µg based on the preclinical no-observed-adverse-effect dose. The nonclinical sample size was unreported.
results.detail: The maximum dose was set by formulation solubility and middle-ear volume.
results.quote: starting with the ‘no observed adverse effect level’ dose from our pre-clinical studies

results.finding: The first-in-human LY3056480 trial received regulatory and ethics clearance at 3 sites.
results.detail: The paper identifies the ethics approvals as 17/LO/0632, 83052/2018 and 592/2018AMG1.
results.quote: The trial protocol was approved by national regulatory authorities, medical ethical committees and local R&D authorities

results.finding: In Phase I, 15 adults with sensorineural hearing loss each received 3 intratympanic injections of LY3056480.
In 44 Phase IIa patients with sensorineural hearing loss, the mean treated-ear threshold changed by −0.46 dB at week 12.
results.detail: Untreated ears were assessed in secondary analyses. Some patients improved at individual frequencies, with improvements also observed in untreated ears.
results.quote: the primary endpoint was not met, i.e., the mean pure-tone air-conduction threshold across 2, 4, and 8 kHz did not change from baseline to 12 weeks in the treated ear

results.finding: The Remygen Phase I/II study in longstanding type 1 diabetes randomized 35 participants under approvals from both Swedish authorities.
results.quote: The study was conducted in accordance with the declaration of Helsinki and approved by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (Dnr 2018/200) and the Swedish Medical Products Agency (EudraCT No 2018-001115-73).

results.finding: Among 33 men with longstanding type 1 diabetes who received Remygen, 9 had possibly or probably treatment-related AST elevations.
results.detail: Two participants stopped treatment because of elevated liver transaminases.
results.quote: A total of 9 subjects reported 17 events of elevated AST levels, deemed probably or possibly related to GABA treatment, where 2/33 (those mentioned above) were withdrawn from study treatment.

results.finding: In 33 men analyzed in the Remygen trial, mixed-meal-stimulated C-peptide showed no improvement after 6 months.
results.quote: However, we observed no increase in either fasting- or stimulated C-peptide levels during the 6 months of GABA therapy.

results.finding: In CRFVPTM-treated adult mice, 100% of recorded tdTomato-labeled cardiomyocyte-like cells (n = 7) generated atrial-like action potentials.
results.detail: Baseline staining found no labeled cells expressing the tested cardiomyocyte markers. The constitutive Fsp1 reporter marked multiple resident non-cardiomyocyte populations, so the labeled cells’ electrical activity cannot establish fibroblast origin.
results.quote:
The
tdTomato+ CiCMs that we recorded all generated action
potentials (APs) very similar to atrial cardiomyocytes (Fig. 1c, d).

results.finding: Whole-heart imaging of one CRFVPTM-treated mouse heart classified 2,395 lineage-labeled cells as cardiomyocytes by size.
results.detail: The whole-heart count used cell size, while cardiomyocyte marker co-expression was shown separately in tissue sections. Sarcomere structure and cardiac gene expression support cell identity.
results.quote:
while in one CRFVPTM-treated heart, a total of 806,302 fibroblasts and 2395 tdTomato
+
cardiomyocytes were detected

results.finding: In uninjured adult mice (8 treated, 6 controls), 0.78% of Fsp1-lineage cells in treated hearts were large and α-actinin-positive.
results.detail: Fsp1 also labels other cell types. The authors identify reduced fibrosis and protection of surviving cardiomyocytes as other possible contributors to recovery after infarction.
results.quote:
Approximately 0.78% of the
tdTomato+ cells were α-actinin+ and large in size

results.finding: In hair-cell-ablated mice, CHIR plus valproate restored the translational vestibuloocular reflex at 2 Hz (5 treated, 8 untreated).
results.detail: The in vivo study links hair cell recovery to improved vestibular function. The fate-mapping experiment used drug-treated utricles harvested after ablation, so the origin of the replacement cells in vivo remains inferred.
results.quote:
The substantial regeneration of HCs in the CHV-treated utricles 
at 2 months resulted in restoration of tVOR at 2 Hz.

results.finding: In early Alzheimer’s disease, 61% of allopregnanolone recipients reported adverse events (18 treated among 24 trial completers).
results.quote: AEs were reported by 83% of participants in the placebo arm and 61% of participants in the Allo arm (Table  1 ).

results.finding: In acute ischemic stroke, sovateltide improved the day-90 Barthel Index response versus saline (36 completers, p = 0.0112).
results.detail: Safety was the primary objective. The paper cites neuronal progenitor differentiation in rats and cell cultures. The clinical outcomes cannot determine whether neuron replacement contributed to recovery.
results.quote:
An improvement
on the BI of ≥ 40 points was seen in 64 and 36% of the sovateltide and saline groups, respectively (p = 0.0112; OR 12.44).

results.finding: DAPT-induced mouse cochlear hair cell-like cells (n = 9) had a mean delayed rectifier potassium current of 855 pA.
results.detail: The current is characteristic of immature cochlear hair cells and also occurs in other cell types. The study assessed lineage and electrophysiology in separate assays.
results.quote: with 855±185 pA (n = 9) for hair cell-like cells, compared to 1302±413 pA (n = 6) for inner hair cells and 853±196 pA (n = 8) for outer hair cells.

definition = "A drug given to a patient would convert cells already present in the affected tissue into a different cell type and restore function lost when cells of that type died. In noise-deafened mice, for example, supporting cells in the inner ear gave rise to new sensory hair cells and hearing partly recovered. The drug induces the change inside the body, without a cell transplant or delivery of genetic reprogramming factors.". Reason: The present tense makes the human capability sound established, while the mouse hearing result shows exactly which part has been demonstrated.

goal.need = "Worldwide, 430 million people need rehabilitation for disabling hearing loss from all causes, including 34 million children. Hearing aids amplify sound for surviving hair cells, yet speech can remain hard to understand in noise. For people whose hearing loss stems from missing hair cells, replacing those cells could restore some ability to detect sound. In type 1 diabetes, enough functioning beta cells could free a person from taking insulin without an islet transplant. Lasting benefit requires the new cells to survive autoimmune attack.". Reason: The transplant history displaces the patient benefit, and the hearing-loss figure needs to be distinguished from the subset attributable to hair-cell loss.

add case "Cardiomyocytes". Reason: Lineage tracing in adult mouse hearts identifies cardiac fibroblasts as a source of chemically induced cardiomyocytes, a replacement cell type absent from the entry.

add milestone after None: "Drug-treated cells in culture acquire the identity and a characteristic function of the target cell.". Reason: The sequence begins in a living animal and omits the earlier demonstration that a drug can change cell identity and function in culture.

edit m1: criterion = "Label the resident source population specifically before drug exposure in a living animal. Identify the label in cells that subsequently express markers of the target type and demonstrate physiological activity characteristic of that type."; set_by = "The lineage-tracing criterion articulated by Leaman, Marichal and Berninger, together with the cell-specific functional comparison used by Ma et al."; set_by_kind = "community_convention"; threshold_quote = "Endogenous starting cell population should be labelled with high specificity before reprogramming, followed by identification of the label in induced cell types"; threshold_ref = 25; refs = [25, 6, 7, 23]. Reason: The criterion gives three study summaries but does not explain how lineage tracing establishes the origin of the new cells.

edit m2: criterion = "In an animal model with a measured deficit caused by cell loss, show that drug treatment produces replacement cells from an identified resident population and that the corresponding physiological function improves relative to controls. Relate the functional improvement to the replacement cells in the affected tissue."; set_by = "Community convention exemplified by Mizutari et al., who assessed the origin of new cochlear hair cells and measured auditory responses in treated and control ears."; set_by_kind = "community_convention"; threshold_quote = "new hair cells can be induced and can cause partial recovery of hearing"; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9, 8]. Reason: The reported frequencies, animal counts and follow-up periods obscure the two observations needed to demonstrate physiological recovery.

add milestone after m2: "Nonclinical safety data support the proposed starting dose and design of the first human study.". Reason: The entry moves directly from animal efficacy to regulatory permission, omitting the nonclinical evidence needed to justify the first human dose.

edit m3: title = "A first human study of a candidate cell-conversion drug has regulatory and ethics clearance."; criterion = "The proposed study may begin under the applicable regulatory and ethics requirements. In the United States, the investigational new drug application must be in effect and the institutional review board must approve the study. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the study on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the study may begin."; set_by = "FDA, Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions, for the US requirements. Other jurisdictions apply their own clinical trial authorization and ethics procedures."; refs = [10, 11, 12]. Reason: The criterion mixes REGAIN’s authorizations with the prospective rule and the title implies the candidate has already been shown to convert human cells.

edit m4: title = "Participants receive a candidate cell-conversion drug in a Phase I safety study."; criterion = "Administer the candidate drug to participants in an authorized Phase I study for the intended cell-replacement use. The study assesses safety and the drug\u2019s pharmacological effects in humans.". Reason: The participant counts and adverse events are study results, while the milestone is reached when people receive the candidate in a safety study.

edit m5: criterion = "A controlled Phase II study in patients with the target condition shows preliminary evidence of effectiveness for the intended cell-replacement indication on its prespecified efficacy endpoint, using the comparator and assessment time defined in the protocol.". Reason: The hearing and diabetes trial outcomes obscure the prospective test for preliminary efficacy in the intended indication.
